title: The Influence of Surgical Assistance Systems on Structure Preservation During Cochlear Electrode Carrier Insertion – A Quasi-Randomized, Single-Blinded Multicenter Study
summary: Despite standardized procedures in cochlear implantation, the surgeon’s technique still significantly affects the quality of outcomes. Factors such as insertion angle and speed can cause structural damage to both the cochlea and vestibular system. Surgical assistance systems—like the CE-certified Otoarm/Otodrive from MED-EL—are designed to precisely control insertion depth, speed, and angle, aiming to minimize insertion trauma and enhance residual hearing preservation. This study compares fully automated insertion with the conventional manual approach regarding their impact on structural preservation.

interventions.name: Electrode Array Insertion Assisted by Otoarm/Otodrive

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- German as native language
- postlingual deafness
- implantation with FLEXsoft electrode array (MED-EL) possible
Exclusion criteria:
-active neurological/psychiatric diagnoses
- vestibular schwannoma
- meningitis
- labyrinthitis
- cochlear malformation
- cochleostomy
- inability to comply with study instructions
- inability to receive implantation with the FLEXsoft electrode array (MED-EL)
